blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top, AI ethics cannot be delegated. Whichever AI systems a company puts into production eventually reflect the values of the leaders who approved them. When something goes wrong — when the system quietly treats some customers unfairly, or uses data the owner never agreed to, or produces an output the company cannot explain — the conversation reaches the executive team very quickly.

Provided that senior leaders stay close to the ethical questions at the start, most of the worst outcomes can be avoided before they happen. Although the technical teams can build the controls, the judgement about what 'acceptable' means has to live with the people who will be accountable when something goes public.

Every senior leader who approves an AI project should be able to answer, in plain words, three questions: what is this system deciding, who is affected, and how do we know it is fair? If those answers are unclear, the project is not yet ready for senior approval.

items.q: According to the text, whose values do AI systems in production eventually reflect?
options: The values of the customers who are affected
The values of the vendors who supplied the technology
The values of the leaders who approved them
The values of the technical teams who built the controls
items.why: "AI systems… eventually reflect the values of the leaders who approved them."

items.q: What are the three questions a senior leader should be able to answer?
options: Which vendor supplied it, who owns the data, and who signs off
What could go wrong, who is liable, and how it is insured
What it decides, who is affected, and how we know it is fair
How much it costs, who built it, and when it launches
items.why: "what is this system deciding, who is affected, and how do we know it is fair?"

items.q: The phrase "the judgement about what 'acceptable' means has to live with the people who will be accountable" suggests that…
options: acceptability is a purely technical question
those who bear the consequences must own the ethical decision
ethical judgement can be safely handed to the engineers
the standard for 'acceptable' should be set by regulators alone
items.why: Inferência: a responsabilidade final pertence a quem responderá pelas consequências, não à equipe técnica.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: AI ethics can be outsourced to the technical team as a side task.
Getting involved early prevents most of the worst outcomes.
A project with unclear answers is not ready for approval.
Leaders are accountable when an AI decision goes public.
items.why: Inferência: a tese central é que a ética de IA não pode ser delegada — é responsabilidade executiva.

items.q: What does the text imply about a project whose three answers are unclear?
options: It is not yet mature enough for senior sign-off
It only needs technical, not ethical, review
It should proceed while the answers are refined later
It should be approved with additional monitoring
items.why: Inferência: "If those answers are unclear, the project is not yet ready for senior approval."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando à liderança a folha de aprovação de três perguntas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So this is the sheet. One page, three questions, and no project reaches a senior leader's desk until someone has filled it in. What does the system decide, who is affected, and how do we know it is fair. That's it.

I'll be honest — when I circulated it, a couple of teams thought it was bureaucracy. Then the first project came through, and the person who had to write down 'who is affected' realised she couldn't actually name them. That single blank line sent them back to the data for a week, and the model that came out the other side was far cleaner.

The second project stalled on the fairness question. They had metrics, but nobody could explain them in plain words, which told us the explanation itself wasn't ready. Rather than wave it through, we held it.

What I'd ask of you today is simple. Whichever project lands on your desk, don't sign off until the sheet is complete and you personally understand the three answers. If you can't say them out loud, we're not ready — and that's exactly what this is meant to catch.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte's sheet require before a project reaches a senior leader?
options: A public statement about the system
The three questions filled in on one page
Sign-off from the technical team first
A full budget forecast and a legal opinion
items.why: "One page, three questions, and no project reaches a senior leader's desk until someone has filled it in."

items.q: What happened with the FIRST project that went through the sheet?
options: The fairness metrics were already perfect
The person could not name who was affected, so they went back to the data
It was rejected outright by the board
items.why: "she couldn't actually name them… sent them back to the data for a week."

items.q: Why did the SECOND project stall?
options: Nobody could explain the fairness metrics in plain words
A senior leader refused to read the sheet
items.why: "They had metrics, but nobody could explain them in plain words."

items.q: When Charlotte says "we held it" rather than "wave it through", she implies that…
options: delaying a project is always a failure
an explanation that can't be stated simply isn't yet ready
items.why: Inferência: se não dá para explicar em palavras simples, a própria explicação ainda não está pronta.

items.q: What is the underlying purpose Charlotte attributes to the sheet?
options: To speed up approvals by removing debate
To catch projects where leaders can't articulate the three answers
To shift responsibility onto the technical teams
To create a record for auditors only
items.why: Inferência: "If you can't say them out loud, we're not ready — and that's exactly what this is meant to catch."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Ethics at the top cannot be delegated to a working group." To delegate means to…
options: hand a task or authority to someone else
items.why: To delegate = delegar: passar uma tarefa ou autoridade a outra pessoa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When a leader is ___ for an AI decision, they answer for it when it goes public."
items.why: Accountable = responsável: quem responde pelo resultado publicamente.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The system used data the customer never ___, which raised an immediate consent problem."
items.why: To agree to = concordar com: o cliente nunca deu consentimento para o uso dos dados.

items.q: "Explain it in plain words before you ask for sign-off." This phrase means…
options: in simple, clear language anyone can follow
items.why: Plain words = palavras simples: linguagem clara, sem jargão.

items.q: The systems a company deploys eventually reflect the values of its leaders. This means they…
options: mirror the priorities and standards leaders chose
items.why: To reflect values = refletir valores: os sistemas espelham as prioridades de quem os aprovou.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre governança de IA. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "No senior leader should sign off on a project until the sheet is complete." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two teams pushed back on the sheet, calling it bureaucracy." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Rather than wave it through, Charlotte held the project." To wave something through means to…
items.why: Wave through = aprovar sem o devido escrutínio, deixar passar.

items.q: "They agreed to fix the metrics but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A vague fairness statement won't hold up once the decision goes public." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = resistir ao escrutínio, manter-se válido quando questionado.
